# [Unreleased](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/)

## Bug fixes

- Step and experiment times given as strings, such as `"Rest for -5 minutes"` or `"0 seconds"`, now raise `ValueError: time must be positive`, as numeric times already did. Before, they gave a negative or zero duration or period. Step temperatures can now be NumPy scalars (e.g. `np.int64(298)`), which used to raise an `AttributeError`. ([#5920](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/issues/5920), [#5923](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5923))
- `IDAKLUSolver.jaxify` now returns correct derivatives at any requested time. Before, it dropped negative tangents and scalar-time cotangents, and read sensitivities from the wrong solver step, or from the nearest `t_eval` point at off-grid times. ([#5916](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5916))
  - Inputs are looked up by name, so key order or an `OrderedDict` no longer swaps their values, and a call with other keys no longer breaks earlier `jax.jit` functions. Missing inputs raise a `SolverError`.
  - Input values may be JAX or size-1 arrays of any numeric dtype, and their derivatives keep that shape; larger arrays raise a `SolverError`. Before, integer and `float32` inputs were misread under `jax.jit`.
  - `get_var` and `get_vars` now use the function they are given.
  - `jax.vmap` over tangent directions returns one result per direction, and over time shares one solve.
  - Times outside the solution, and derivatives with respect to time, give NaN rather than an error or a wrong value.
- `pybamm` now installs on Python 3.15. `pybammsolvers` 0.11.0 declared `requires-python <3.15` and shipped no cp315 wheels, so `pybamm`'s solver requirement could not be met there. Released `pybammsolvers` v0.11.1, which allows Python 3.15 and ships cp315 wheels. ([#5909](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5909))

# [v26.10.1.1](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/tree/pybamm-v26.10.1.1) - 2026-10-19

## Bug fixes

- `set_initial_state` without a `direction` now keeps a user-set `"Initial hysteresis state in {electrode} electrode"` and solves the initial stoichiometries on the OCP at that state, `(1 + h0) / 2 * U_delith + (1 - h0) / 2 * U_lith`. Before, it reset the state to 0 and solved on `"{Electrode} electrode OCP [V]"`, so a hysteresis model started at h = 0 and, when that OCP differed from the branch average, away from the requested voltage. With h0 = 0 the initial stoichiometries now come from the branch average rather than `"OCP [V]"`. ([#5928](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5928))

# [v26.10.1.0](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/tree/pybamm-v26.10.1.0) - 2026-10-13

## Features

- `FiniteVolume` has a `"harmonic flux coefficients"` option, off by default. When it is on, a node-valued coefficient multiplying a sum of gradient terms, such as the electrolyte conductivity in `kappa * (chi * grad(c_e) - grad(phi_e))`, takes the distance-weighted harmonic mean on faces, not only one multiplying a single `grad`. With the arithmetic mean, the coefficient jump at the electrode/separator interface makes the DFN first order in x; with the option on, it converges at second order. ([#5856](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5856))
- Added support for Python 3.15 to `pybamm` and `pybammsolvers`. On 3.15, the `vtk` extra installs nothing until cp315 wheels are available for it. ([#5762](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5762))
- The `jax` extra now accepts JAX up to 0.11 (previously below 0.9), which brings `JaxSolver` and the IDAKLU-JAX interface to Python 3.15. JAX 0.11 needs Python 3.12 or newer, so Python 3.11 gets JAX 0.10 at most. ([#5762](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5762))
- A `fem` extra installs the finite-element meshing dependencies, scikit-fem and meshio, so `pip install "pybamm[fem]"` is enough for 2D and 3D finite-element meshes. `pybamm[all]` includes it. ([#5881](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5881))
- `ParameterValues.update` takes `strict=True`, which raises a `KeyError` naming the closest existing parameters when a key does not exist, and then updates nothing. The default (`strict=False`) still adds new parameters. ([#5874](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/issues/5874), [#5886](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5886))
- Benchmarks now time import, solver set-up and the first variable read, track how cost scales with problem size, and fail if a run stops early. ([#5903](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5903))

## Bug fixes

- `IDAKLUSolver` no longer fails to converge when the AMD-ordered KLU factorisation picks a weak pivot. KLU now rejects pivots smaller than 0.1 of the largest entry in their column, instead of 0.001. The new `klu_pivot_tolerance` option of `IDAKLUSolver` and `NonlinearSolver` sets this tolerance, from just above 0 up to 1 (full partial pivoting). ([#5904](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5904))
- `"intercalation kinetics": "Marcus"` now gives a positive current for a positive overpotential, as the other kinetics do, and converts the reorganization energy from eV with F/RT, as Marcus-Hush-Chidsey does. Previously the oxidation and reduction terms were swapped and the energy was used in mixed units, so models with Marcus kinetics failed to solve. ([#5872](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5872))
- Evaluating a processed variable at a 0-d array time, e.g. `solution["Voltage [V]"](np.array(10.0))`, now returns the same value as passing the float rather than raising an `IndexError`. ([#5762](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5762))
- Fixed the particle concentration of the `"quartic profile"` particle model in models that resolve the electrode (e.g. DFN), which was missing a factor of the particle radius on the concentration gradient term and diverged to unphysical values. ([#5893](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5893))
- `EffectiveResistance` and `AlternativeEffectiveResistance2D` `post_process` no longer return NaN for the voltage and positive current collector potential at times after the current collector problem was solved. ([#5858](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5858))
- `"Maximum/Minimum {domain} particle stoichiometry"` and the matching concentration variables now include the particle surface value. Before, they only used cell-centre values, so the maximum could be lower than the maximum surface stoichiometry during charge. ([#5842](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5842))
- `Ai2020`'s electrolyte diffusivity now converts the Valoen and Reimers (2005) fit from cm2/s to m2/s. It was 1e4 times too large, so DFN simulations with Ai2020 had almost no electrolyte concentration gradient. ([#5887](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/issues/5887), [#5888](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5888))
- `Chayambuka2022`'s NVPF (positive electrode) diffusivity is now looked up at the solid concentration, `sto * c_max`, instead of `sto` times the initial electrolyte concentration, which made it 20 to 50 times too large. ([#5885](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/issues/5885), [#5889](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5889))
- Fixed the 1+1D and 2+1D potential pair current collector models ignoring `"Number of electrodes connected in parallel to make a cell"`. The tab boundary condition now uses the current through one electrode pair instead of the whole cell current. ([#5826](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5826))

# [v26.10.0.0](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/tree/pybamm-v26.10.0.0) - 2026-10-09

## Breaking changes

- `pybamm` now requires `pybammsolvers>=0.11.0`, for the IDAKLU solver statistics and self-scheduled input-set sweeps. Upgrade `pybammsolvers` together with `pybamm`. ([#5782](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5782))
- `Symbol.children`, `Symbol.domain` (and `secondary_domain`, `tertiary_domain`, `quaternary_domain`) and `FunctionParameter.input_names` return immutable tuples that compare equal to lists, and `Symbol.domains` returns a read-only copy, as do `to_json()`, `get_children_domains()`, `read_domain_or_domains()` and `pybamm.EMPTY_DOMAINS`. Editing them raises `TypeError` instead of emitting `SymbolMutationDeprecationWarning`, and not even `list` or `dict` methods can change a symbol through them. This ends the deprecation of these edits early; before 26.9 they left the symbol's identity stale. The sequences are no longer `list` instances and slicing them gives a plain tuple; tuples are accepted wherever domains are given. Build a new symbol with `with_domains`, `create_copy(new_children=...)` or `pybamm.replace`. The deprecated setters (`name`, `domains`, `scale`, ...) are unchanged. ([#5825](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5825))
- `Solution` and `EISSolution` no longer have an instance `__dict__`, so attributes they do not define cannot be attached to them. Subclass `pybamm.Solution` to add attributes. A solution pickled with an attached attribute still loads, without that attribute and with a logged warning. ([#5827](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5827))

## Deprecated

- Setting `Array.entries_string` or `Interpolant.entries_string`, and calling `StateVector.set_evaluation_array`, are in-place symbol updates and now emit `SymbolMutationDeprecationWarning`. Construct a new symbol instead. ([#5825](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5825))
- `ProcessedVariable`'s `base_variables_casadi` argument and attribute are deprecated; pass the CasADi functions positionally or as `observer=`, and call the variable to evaluate it. ([#5786](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5786))
- Setting `model.convert_to_format = None` is deprecated and raises a `DeprecationWarning`. `None` was documented as keeping the PyBaMM expression tree, but it has evaluated the same way as `"python"` since 2022. Set `convert_to_format = "python"` instead, or leave the default. ([#5784](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5784))

## Features

- `FiniteVolumeUnstructured` accepts anisotropic coefficients in `div(K * grad(u))`: a `VectorField` with one value per axis (a diagonal tensor, as `FiniteVolume2D` takes) or a rank-2 `TensorField` (the full tensor), each component a cell field. Each face uses its normal conductivity n·K·n from the cells on either side, combined by the same distance-weighted harmonic mean as a scalar coefficient, which is exact when the principal axes of K are aligned with the faces; the tangential part of K n is not included. Previously a `VectorField` coefficient raised `DiscretisationError`. ([#5835](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5835))
- `Solution.solver_statistics` reports the integrator's step, linear-solver-setup, nonlinear-iteration, nonlinear-failure and error-test-failure counts as a `pybamm.SolverStatistics` dataclass. `IDAKLUSolver` fills it for every solution, counting across `t_eval` breakpoints and separately for each input set, and the counts are summed when solutions are combined, so a stepped or experiment solution reports its total, including the cycles that `save_at_cycles` does not keep. ([#5782](https://github.com/pybamm-team/PyBaMM/pull/5782))

    def test_discontinuity_events_different_times_error(self):
        # Test that an error is raised when discontinuity events occur at different
        # times for different input parameter sets
        model = pybamm.BaseModel()
        v = pybamm.Variable("v")
        t_event = pybamm.InputParameter("t_event")
        model.rhs = {v: pybamm.t > t_event}
        model.initial_conditions = {v: 0}
        model.variables = {"v": v}

        disc = pybamm.Discretisation()
        disc.process_model(model)

        solver = pybamm.BaseSolver()
        t_eval = np.linspace(0, 10)

        # Different input sets with discontinuities at different times
        inputs_list = [{"t_event": 3.0}, {"t_event": 5.0}]

        with pytest.raises(
            pybamm.SolverError,
            match="Discontinuity events occur at different times between input parameter sets",
        ):

        expected = np.array([1.0, 3.0, 5.0])

        # Exclusive of endpoints
        t_eval_endpoints = [t_eval[0], t_eval[-1]]
        assert all(t not in result for t in t_eval_endpoints)

        np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)

I'm checking a test about discontinuity events at different times, where BaseSolver should raise an error for inputs 3.0 and 5.0, and I'm wondering whether that expectation still holds. I'm also trying to pin down the bug: it seems to happen when two input sets put their discontinuity on a t_eval point, maybe at 5.0 for both.

Now I'm checking whether the IDAKLU path handles input-dependent discontinuities: an `InputParameter` probably isn't constant, so those discontinuities get routed through the segment logic in `BaseSolver.solve`, which restarts from the initial conditions instead of the last state. That looks like the first bug.

I'm working through the bug list for the discontinuity handling: the C++ IDAKLU solver can't take per-input-set t_eval points, so the error for differing discontinuity times stays. I still need to fix the loop that stops all input sets when the first one hits a non-final termination, and add discontinuity handling inside `step()`.

Now I'm going through the experiment model change sensitivities: `_set_sens_initial_conditions_from` subtracts the reference from the sensitivity, which is wrong because a constant offset has zero derivative, and it also accesses `var.scale.value`, which breaks when the scale depends on an input.

Now I'm checking how the sensitivity initial conditions are built from the experiment's state mappers, since a mapper's derivative should include both the old state's sensitivity and the direct parameter term rather than the current reference subtraction. I'm also looking at a second bug: when one solve continues from a previous `["a"]` solution into a new `["b"]` solver, the sensitivities are pulled from `_all_sensitivities["all"][0]`, which may not match what the new model expects.

Now I'm looking at a sensitivity bug in `step()`: the RuntimeError is raised when `calculate_sensitivities` changes between calls, and I'm checking which branch triggers it. I also need the continuation path to look up sensitivities by input name rather than by position, and to raise a SolverError naming any missing inputs.

Now I'm sorting out the remaining bugs: the RuntimeError when sensitivities change between `step()` calls, and the fact that `calculate_sensitivities` gets set before that check, so a failed call still leaves it changed. I'll defer that assignment until after the check. I also need to stop each set-up from adding another copy of the discontinuity events to `model.events`, while keeping any discontinuity events the user added themselves.

I'm deciding how to avoid duplicating the discontinuity events on each set-up: I'm planning to skip adding an event when one with the same name and expression is already present, which still lets extra events be added for a longer t_eval. I'm also checking how Modulo events change with input-dependent periods when the expression isn't constant.

I'm working out how to handle Modulo discontinuities when the period is an input, since the current approach of pre-creating a fixed number of events from `tf // expr.value` breaks for an `InputParameter`. I'm considering instead computing the reset times directly from the `t_eval` range and each input set's period, so the resets follow whatever the inputs give.

I'm weighing whether a Modulo period that depends on time can be rejected cleanly, and which error type fits best. I'm also checking whether the casadi solver relies on the Modulo discontinuity events that are currently stored in `model.events`.

I'm checking whether the constant-time Modulo discontinuities should be generated from the `t_eval` range at evaluation time rather than from a fixed event count set at set-up, so that resets aren't missed for later times.

I'm checking whether `_get_discontinuity_start_end_indices` is called anywhere besides the solver itself, since the signature I'd keep must still return the same start indices, end indices and t_eval.

Now I'm checking how the IDAKLU C++ solver handles discontinuities at t_eval points, to see whether it reinitializes at each one or only at the event times.

I'm checking how the C++ IDAKLU solver handles t_eval points, since that decides whether integer t_eval arrays and per-segment t_interp slicing need fixing in the segment loop.

    def _segment_series(s, repeated, hermite, t_evals):
        """Series lists for one segment, dropping the leading sample when
        ``repeated`` (its first time point duplicates the running boundary).
        Shared by ``__add__`` and ``from_sub_solutions``."""
        first = slice(1, None) if repeated else slice(None)
        ts = [s.all_ts[0][first], *s.all_ts[1:]]
        ys = [s.all_ys[0][:, first], *s.all_ys[1:]]
        yps = [s.all_yps[0][:, first], *s.all_yps[1:]] if hermite else None
        tev = [s._all_t_evals[0][first], *s._all_t_evals[1:]] if t_evals else None

    @staticmethod
    def _merge_sensitivities(acc, s, repeated):
        """Fold one segment's sensitivities into the running dict ``acc``,
        dropping the leading time point's rows when ``repeated``."""
        for key, (first, *rest) in s._all_sensitivities.items():
            # Rows are time-major, one block per time point, as in _segment_series
            rows_repeated = len(first) // len(s.all_ts[0]) if repeated else 0
            acc.setdefault(key, []).extend([first[rows_repeated:], *rest])

    def __add__(self, other):
        """Join ``other`` onto the end of this solution, e.g. when stepping.

        If ``other`` starts after this solution ends, an ``ExplicitTimeIntegral``
        integrates across the gap, interpolating its integrand linearly there. If
        either solution returned output variables only, the integral is instead
        the sum of the integrals over each solution, so the gap adds nothing.

        Parameters
        ----------
        other : :class:`pybamm.Solution` or None
            The solution to append.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`pybamm.Solution`
            The joined solution.
        """
        if other is None or isinstance(other, EmptySolution):
            return self.copy()
        if not isinstance(other, Solution):
            raise pybamm.SolverError(
                "Only a Solution or None can be added to a Solution"
            )
        # Special case: new solution only has one timestep and it is already in the
        # existing solution. In this case, return a copy of the existing solution
        if (
            len(other.all_ts) == 1
            and len(other.all_ts[0]) == 1
            and other.all_ts[0][0] == self.all_ts[-1][-1]
        ):
            new_sol = self.copy()
            # Update termination using the latter solution
            new_sol._termination = other.termination
            new_sol._t_event = other._t_event
            new_sol._y_event = other._y_event
            new_sol.solver_statistics = _sum_solver_statistics([self, other])
            return new_sol

        # Append other onto self (the already-merged left side); only other's
        # contribution is sliced, keeping accumulation O(N).
        hermite_interpolation = (
            other.hermite_interpolation and self.hermite_interpolation
        )
        t_evals_present = (
            self._all_t_evals is not None and other._all_t_evals is not None
        )
        repeated = other.all_ts[0][0] == self.all_ts[-1][-1]
        ts, ys, yps, tev = self._segment_series(
            other, repeated, hermite_interpolation, t_evals_present
        )
        all_ts = self.all_ts + ts
        all_ys = self.all_ys + ys
        all_yps = self.all_yps + yps if hermite_interpolation else None
        all_t_evals = self._all_t_evals + tev if t_evals_present else None

        # Validate only the newly-joined region (self's last segment + other's
        # contribution), not the whole accumulation. self's earlier segments
        # were already validated when self was built, so this stays O(size of
        # other) per add, i.e. O(N) total instead of O(N^2).
        n = len(self.all_ts)
        self._ensure_sorted_t([self.all_ts[-1], *all_ts[n:]], "all_ts")
        if all_t_evals is not None:
            self._ensure_t_evals(
                all_ts=[self.all_ts[-1], *all_ts[n:]],
                all_t_evals=[self._all_t_evals[-1], *all_t_evals[n:]],
            )

        # sensitivities are a dict of {parameter: [sensitivities]}; start from a
        # fresh copy of self's lists so the in-place merge never aliases them
        all_sensitivities = {
            key: list(value) for key, value in self._all_sensitivities.items()
        }
        self._merge_sensitivities(all_sensitivities, other, repeated)

        options = self.user_options | other.user_options

        new_sol = Solution(
            all_ts,
            all_ys,
            self.all_models + other.all_models,
            self.all_inputs + other.all_inputs,
            other.t_event,
            other.y_event,
            other.termination,
            all_sensitivities=all_sensitivities,
            all_yps=all_yps,
            all_t_evals=all_t_evals,
            variables_returned=other.variables_returned,
            options=options,
            _validate_time_structure=False,
        )

        new_sol.closest_event_idx = other.closest_event_idx
        new_sol._y0 = self._y0
        new_sol._y0_sensitivities = self._y0_sensitivities
        new_sol._y_event_sensitivities = other._y_event_sensitivities
        new_sol._all_inputs_stacked = self.all_inputs_stacked + other.all_inputs_stacked
        new_sol._all_inputs_casadi = self.all_inputs_casadi + other.all_inputs_casadi

        # Add timers (if available)
        for attr in ["solve_time", "integration_time", "set_up_time"]:
            if (
                getattr(self, attr, None) is not None
                and getattr(other, attr, None) is not None
            ):
                setattr(new_sol, attr, getattr(self, attr) + getattr(other, attr))
        new_sol.solver_statistics = _sum_solver_statistics([self, other])

        # Set sub_solutions
        new_sol._sub_solutions = self.sub_solutions + other.sub_solutions

        # update variables which were derived at the solver stage
        if any([self.variables_returned, other.variables_returned]):

            new_sol._variables = {v: self[v].update(other[v], new_sol) for v in vars}
            new_sol.variables_returned = True

        return new_sol

        model = pybamm.BaseModel()
        var1 = pybamm.Variable("var1")

        a = 0.6

        model.initial_conditions = {var1: 0, var2: 0}

        step_solver = pybamm.CasadiSolver(rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-8)

        sol = solver.solve(

            calculate_sensitivities=["b"],

        # dw/db = c = e^-t; a is not a sensitivity input, so it has no entry

def _get_discontinuity_start_end_indices(self, model, y0, inputs, t_eval):
        if self.supports_t_eval_discontinuities and model.t_discon_constant_symbols:
            pybamm.logger.verbose("Discontinuity events found for constant symbols")
            _t_discon_constant = []
            for symbol, expr, num_events in model.t_discon_constant_symbols:
                _t_discon_constant.extend(
                    symbol._t_discon(expr, y0, inputs, num_events)
                )

            t_discon_constant = self.filter_discontinuities(_t_discon_constant, t_eval)
            t_eval = np.union1d(t_eval, t_discon_constant)

        if not model.discontinuity_events_eval:
            pybamm.logger.verbose("No additional discontinuity events found")
            return [0], [len(t_eval)], t_eval

        # Calculate all possible discontinuities
        _t_discon_full = [
            event.expression.evaluate(inputs=inputs)
            for event in model.discontinuity_events_eval
        ]
        t_discon = self.filter_discontinuities(_t_discon_full, t_eval)

        pybamm.logger.verbose(f"Discontinuity events found at t = {t_discon}")

        # insert time points around discontinuities in t_eval
        # keep track of subsections to integrate by storing start and end indices
        start_indices = [0]
        end_indices = []
        eps = sys.float_info.epsilon
        for dtime in t_discon:
            dindex = np.searchsorted(t_eval, dtime, side="left")
            end_indices.append(dindex + 1)
            start_indices.append(dindex + 1)
            if dtime * (1 - eps) < t_eval[dindex] < dtime * (1 + eps):
                t_eval[dindex] *= 1 + eps
                t_eval = np.insert(t_eval, dindex, dtime * (1 - eps))
            else:
                t_eval = np.insert(
                    t_eval, dindex, [dtime * (1 - eps), dtime * (1 + eps)]
                )
        end_indices.append(len(t_eval))

        return start_indices, end_indices, t_eval

            The period, which may depend on input parameters.
        y0 : array-like
            The state at ``t_eval[0]``.
        inputs : dict
            Input parameters for one input set.
        t_eval : :class:`numpy.ndarray`
            The integration window.

        Returns
        -------
        :class:`numpy.ndarray`
            The reset times, empty for an infinite or zero period.
        """
        period = np.abs(np.asarray(expr.evaluate(0, y0, inputs=inputs), dtype=float))
        if period.size != 1:
            raise pybamm.SolverError(
                f"The period of a Modulo must be a scalar, not of shape {period.shape}"
            )
        period = period.item()
        if not np.isfinite(period) or period == 0:
            return np.empty(0)
        first = np.floor(t_eval[0] / period)
        last = np.floor(t_eval[-1] / period) + 1
        return np.arange(first, last + 1) * period

    def _get_discontinuity_start_end_indices(self, model, y0, inputs, t_eval):
        """Split ``t_eval`` into the segments to integrate between discontinuities.

        Time-constant discontinuities that the solver handles as breakpoints in
        ``t_eval`` are inserted into it; every other discontinuity in the window
        ends one segment just before it and starts the next just after it.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : :class:`pybamm.BaseModel`
            The set-up model.
        y0 : array-like
            The state at ``t_eval[0]``.
        inputs : dict
            Input parameters for one input set.
        t_eval : array-like
            The integration times, which are not modified.

        Returns
        -------
        start_indices : list of int
            Index in the returned ``t_eval`` of the first time of each segment.
        end_indices : list of int
            Index in the returned ``t_eval`` just after the last time of each
            segment.
        t_eval : :class:`numpy.ndarray`
            The integration times, as floats, with the discontinuity times added.
        """
        t_eval = np.array(t_eval, dtype=float).reshape(-1)

        breakpoints = []
        split_times = []
        for symbol, expr, num_events in model.t_discon_constant_symbols:
            as_breakpoints = self.supports_t_eval_discontinuities and expr.is_constant()
            if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Modulo):
                times = self._modulo_reset_times(expr, y0, inputs, t_eval)
                if as_breakpoints:
                    # Stop right before each reset and at it
                    breakpoints.extend(np.nextafter(times, -np.inf))
                    breakpoints.extend(times)
                else:
                    split_times.extend(times)
            else:
                breakpoints.extend(symbol._t_discon(expr, y0, inputs, num_events))

        if breakpoints:
            pybamm.logger.verbose("Discontinuity events found for constant symbols")
            t_eval = np.union1d(
                t_eval, self.filter_discontinuities(breakpoints, t_eval)
            )

        split_times.extend(
            np.ravel(event.expression.evaluate(inputs=inputs))
            for event in model.discontinuity_events_eval
        )
        if not split_times:
            pybamm.logger.verbose("No additional discontinuity events found")
            return [0], [len(t_eval)], t_eval

        t_discon = self.filter_discontinuities(np.hstack(split_times), t_eval)
        pybamm.logger.verbose(f"Discontinuity events found at t = {t_discon}")

        # Each segment ends just before a discontinuity and the next starts just
        # after it. One within a float of an end of t_eval, or of the previous
        # discontinuity, leaves no room for a segment, so it is not split on.
        eps = sys.float_info.epsilon
        lefts = []
        rights = []
        for dtime in t_discon:
            candidates = (dtime * (1 - eps), dtime * (1 + eps))
            left = min(*candidates, np.nextafter(dtime, -np.inf))
            right = max(*candidates, np.nextafter(dtime, np.inf))
            previous = rights[-1] if rights else t_eval[0]
            if left <= previous or right >= t_eval[-1]:
                continue
            lefts.append(left)
            rights.append(right)

        if not lefts:
            return [0], [len(t_eval)], t_eval

        # Drop the requested times within a float of a discontinuity
        lefts = np.array(lefts)
        rights = np.array(rights)
        index = np.searchsorted(rights, t_eval, side="left")
        inside = (index < len(lefts)) & (
            t_eval >= lefts[np.minimum(index, len(lefts) - 1)]
        )
        t_eval = np.sort(np.concatenate([t_eval[~inside], lefts, rights]))

        start_indices = [0, *np.searchsorted(t_eval, rights).tolist()]
        end_indices = [*(np.searchsorted(t_eval, lefts) + 1).tolist(), len(t_eval)]
        return start_indices, end_indices, t_eval

I also need to keep in mind that the modulo split times can fall outside the range, which the filter step already handles. For the inside mask, I'm finding the first interval whose right edge is at or past each evaluation point and checking it against the left edge, which works because the intervals don't overlap.

I'm checking whether `model.t_discon_constant_symbols` might be missing on some models, since the original code only reached it when the solver supports discontinuities, so a BaseSolver mock could break. I'm thinking about using `getattr` with a default of an empty list to make it safe.

I'm reasoning through the Modulo split times: with a constant period, the reset points run up to the end time, and I want to confirm the boundary filter excludes the right values at the endpoint.

def _integrate_segments(
        self,
        model,
        t_eval,
        start_indices,
        end_indices,
        inputs_list,
        t_interp,
        nproc,
        timer,

        """Integrate each input set across the segments between discontinuities.

        Each input set restarts every segment from the state and sensitivities
        it reached at the end of the previous one, and stops at the first
        segment it does not integrate to the end of.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : :class:`pybamm.BaseModel`
            The set-up model, initialised for every input set.
        t_eval : :class:`numpy.ndarray`
            The integration times of all the segments.
        start_indices, end_indices : list of int
            The bounds of each segment in ``t_eval``.
        inputs_list : list of dict
            Input parameters for each input set.
        t_interp : :class:`numpy.ndarray`
            The interpolation times, possibly empty.
        nproc : int or None
            Number of processes to integrate the input sets with.
        timer : :class:`pybamm.Timer`
            The timer that the segments' solve times are read from.

        Returns
        -------
        list of :class:`pybamm.Solution`
            One solution per input set.
        """
        solutions = [None] * len(inputs_list)
        active = list(range(len(inputs_list)))
        new_solutions = []
        for start_index, end_index in zip(start_indices, end_indices, strict=True):
            t_segment = t_eval[start_index:end_index]
            active_inputs = [inputs_list[i] for i in active]
            if start_index != start_indices[0]:
                self._restart_from_solutions(
                    model, t_segment[0], new_solutions, active_inputs
                )
            pybamm.logger.verbose(
                f"Calling solver for {t_segment[0]} < t < {t_segment[-1]}"
            )
            new_solutions = self._integrate(
                model,
                t_segment,
                active_inputs,
                self._segment_t_interp(t_interp, t_segment),
                nproc=nproc,
            )
            # pybamm.Solution.__add__ assumes attribute solve_time.
            solve_time = timer.time()
            for i, new_solution in zip(active, new_solutions, strict=True):
                new_solution.solve_time = solve_time
                if solutions[i] is None:
                    solutions[i] = new_solution
                else:
                    solutions[i] = solutions[i] + new_solution

            still_active = [
                k
                for k, i in enumerate(active)
                if solutions[i].termination == "final time"

            active = [active[k] for k in still_active]

    def _set_sens_initial_conditions_from(
        self, solution: pybamm.Solution, model: pybamm.BaseModel
    ) -> tuple:
        """
        A restricted version of BaseModel.set_initial_conditions_from that only extracts the
        sensitivities from a solution object, and only for a model that has been discretised.
        This is used when setting the initial conditions for a sensitivity model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        solution : :class:`pybamm.Solution`
            The solution to use to initialize the model

        model: :class:`pybamm.BaseModel`
            The model whose sensitivities to set

        Returns
        -------

        initial_conditions : tuple of ndarray
            The initial conditions for the sensitivities, each element of the tuple
            corresponds to an input parameter
        """

        ninputs = len(model.calculate_sensitivities)
        initial_conditions = tuple([] for _ in range(ninputs))
        solution = solution.last_state
        for var in model.initial_conditions:
            final_state = solution[var.name]
            final_state = final_state.sensitivities
            final_state_eval = tuple(
                final_state[key] for key in model.calculate_sensitivities
            )

            scale, reference = var.scale.value, var.reference.value
            for i in range(ninputs):
                scaled_final_state_eval = (final_state_eval[i] - reference) / scale
                initial_conditions[i].append(scaled_final_state_eval)

        # Also update the concatenated initial conditions if the model is already
        # discretised
        # Unpack slices for sorting
        y_slices = {var: slce for var, slce in model.y_slices.items()}
        slices = [y_slices[symbol][0] for symbol in model.initial_conditions]

        # sort equations according to slices
        concatenated_initial_conditions = [
            casadi.vertcat(*[eq for _, eq in sorted(zip(slices, init, strict=True))])
            for init in initial_conditions
        ]

    def _mapped_state_sensitivities(
        mapper_func, time, last_state, mapper_inputs: dict, names
    ) -> tuple:
        """Sensitivities of the states that ``mapper_func`` maps a final state to.

        By the chain rule, ``dy0/dp = df/dy @ dy/dp + df/dp``, where ``y`` is the
        final state of ``last_state`` and ``f`` may depend on ``p`` directly.

        Parameters
        ----------
        mapper_func : :class:`casadi.Function`
            The map ``f(t, y, p)`` to the new initial states, with ``p`` stacked
            as in ``mapper_inputs``.
        time : float
            The time to evaluate the map at.
        last_state : :class:`pybamm.Solution`
            The final state that is mapped.
        mapper_inputs : dict
            The values of ``p``, in the order ``mapper_func`` stacks them.
        names : list of str
            The inputs to differentiate with respect to.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple of :class:`numpy.ndarray`
            The sensitivities of the new initial states, one per name.
        """
        y_from = last_state.all_ys[0]
        dy_from = BaseSolver._state_sensitivities_by_name(last_state, names)
        p = stack_inputs(mapper_inputs)
        _, jac_y, jac_p = mapper_func.jacobian()(
            time, y_from, p, mapper_func(time, y_from, p)
        )

        columns = {}
        start = 0
        for name, value in mapper_inputs.items():
            columns[name] = (start, np.size(value))
            start += np.size(value)

        sensitivities = []
        for name, dy in zip(names, dy_from, strict=True):
            dy0 = jac_y @ casadi.DM(dy)
            if name in columns:
                start, size = columns[name]
                if size != 1:
                    raise pybamm.SolverError(
                        f"Cannot calculate sensitivities to the input '{name}' of "
                        f"size {size}, only to scalar inputs"
                    )
                dy0 += jac_p[:, start]
            sensitivities.append(np.asarray(dy0.full()).reshape(-1))
        return tuple(sensitivities)

    def _set_sens_initial_conditions_from(
        self,
        solution: pybamm.Solution,
        model: pybamm.BaseModel,
        inputs: dict | None = None,
    ) -> tuple:
        """
        Sensitivities of the initial states that
        :meth:`pybamm.BaseModel.set_initial_conditions_from` gives a discretised
        model from the final state of a solution.

        Parameters
        ----------
        solution : :class:`pybamm.Solution`
            The solution to use to initialize the model
        model: :class:`pybamm.BaseModel`
            The model whose sensitivities to set
        inputs : dict, optional
            The input parameters of ``model``.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple of :class:`numpy.ndarray`
            The initial conditions for the sensitivities, each element of the tuple
            corresponds to an input parameter
        """
        inputs = inputs or {}
        last_state = solution.last_state
        previous_model = last_state.all_models[-1]
        mapper = model.build_initial_state_mapper(previous_model)

        # The map involves the inputs of both models, through their scales and
        # references and any variable of the previous model it reads
        previous_inputs = last_state.all_inputs[0]
        names = sorted(
            {
                symbol.name
                for symbol in mapper.pre_order()
                if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.InputParameter)
            }
        )
        mapper_inputs = {
            name: inputs[name] if name in inputs else previous_inputs[name]
            for name in names

        y_casadi = casadi.MX.sym("y", previous_model.len_rhs_and_alg)
        p_casadi = {
            name: casadi.MX.sym(name, np.size(value))
            for name, value in mapper_inputs.items()

            "mapper",

            [mapper.to_casadi(t_casadi, y_casadi, inputs=p_casadi)],
        )
        return self._mapped_state_sensitivities(
            mapper_func,
            last_state.all_ts[-1][-1],
            last_state,
            mapper_inputs,
            model.calculate_sensitivities,
        )

    def test_solve_with_sensitivities_and_experiment(self, solver_cls):
        experiment_2step = pybamm.Experiment(
            [
                (
                    "Discharge at C/20 for 2 min",
                    "Charge at 1 A for 1 min",
                    "Hold at 4.1 V for 1 min",
                    "Discharge at 2 W for 1 min",
                    "Discharge at 2 W for 1 min",  # repeat to cover this case (changes initialisation)
                ),
            ]
            * 2,
        )

        solutions = []
        input_param_name = "Negative electrode active material volume fraction"
        solver = pybamm.IDAKLUSolver(atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-8)
        for calculate_sensitivities in [False, True]:
            model = solver_cls()
            param = model.default_parameter_values
            input_param_value = param[input_param_name]
            param.update({input_param_name: "[input]"})
            sim = pybamm.Simulation(
                model,
                experiment=experiment_2step,
                solver=solver,
                parameter_values=param,
            )
            solution = sim.solve(
                inputs={input_param_name: input_param_value},
                calculate_sensitivities=calculate_sensitivities,
            )
            solutions.append(solution)

        model = solver_cls()
        param = model.default_parameter_values
        base_input_param_value = param[input_param_name]
        fd_tol = 1e-4
        for dh in [-fd_tol, fd_tol]:
            model = solver_cls()
            param = model.default_parameter_values
            input_param_value = base_input_param_value * (1.0 + dh)
            param.update({input_param_name: "[input]"})
            sim = pybamm.Simulation(
                model,
                experiment=experiment_2step,
                solver=solver,
                parameter_values=param,
            )
            solution = sim.solve(
                inputs={input_param_name: input_param_value},
            )
            solutions.append(solution)

        # check solutions are the same
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            solutions[0]["Voltage [V]"].data,
            solutions[1]["Voltage [V]"](solutions[0].t),
            rtol=5e-2,
            equal_nan=True,
        )
        sensitivity_keys = set(solutions[1]["Voltage [V]"].sensitivities)
        assert input_param_name in sensitivity_keys
        assert pybamm.Simulation._STEP_INDEX_INPUT not in sensitivity_keys

        # use finite difference to check sensitivities
        t = solutions[0].t
        soln_neg = solutions[2]["Voltage [V]"](t)
        soln_pos = solutions[3]["Voltage [V]"](t)
        sens_fd = (soln_pos - soln_neg) / (2 * fd_tol * base_input_param_value)
        sens_idaklu = np.interp(
            t,
            solutions[1].t,
            solutions[1]["Voltage [V]"].sensitivities[input_param_name].flatten(),
        )
        np.testing.assert_allclose(
            sens_fd,
            sens_idaklu,
            rtol=2e-4,
            atol=2e-3,
        )

arguments.message:
All seven restart problems are fixed in `solvers/base_solver.py` and `solvers/idaklu_solver.py`. The existing solver, simulation and experiment tests pass, except for ones that fail on the original code too: those that download data (no network here), a LaTeX preview test, and a few that crash or run out of memory when run in parallel. The VTK plotting tests segfault in this headless environment.

**What was wrong, briefly:** IDAKLU starts from `model.y0full`, which was never updated between segments, so every later segment restarted from the initial conditions. The segment loop also only checked whether the first input set had stopped. `step()` ignored discontinuities completely. Sensitivities carried to a new model did `(sens - reference) / scale.value`: subtracting the reference from a derivative gives the wrong answer, and `.value` doesn't exist on an input-dependent scale.

**Changes:**
1. **Restarts in `solve()`:** both `solve()` and `step()` now go through a shared segment loop. Each input set restarts from its own final state and sensitivities, and stops when it hits an event; the others carry on. `t_interp` is cut to each segment, and the model's initial states are put back afterwards.
2. **Splitting `t_eval`:** `_get_discontinuity_start_end_indices` keeps its signature and return value. It now works on a float copy, so the caller's `t_eval` is untouched and integer arrays work. A discontinuity within a float of a segment boundary is no longer split on, so `t_eval` can't come out out of order.
3. **`step()` and `Modulo`:** `step()` now stops at discontinuities, including `Modulo` resets. Reset times are worked out from the window being integrated and each input set's period. An infinite period never resets, and a period that depends on time (or on the states) raises a `SolverError`.
4. **Duplicate events:** a discontinuity event is only added to `model.events` if it isn't there already.
5. **Change of model:** sensitivities use the chain rule through the state map (`dy0/dp = df/dy · dy/dp + df/dp`), with or without a `state_mapper`. This covers input-dependent scales and references, and states that start from an input directly.
6. **Continuing `step()`:** sensitivities are matched by input name. If the solution being continued has none for a requested input, you get a `SolverError` listing them, e.g. `['b']`.
7. **`calculate_sensitivities`:** changing it between `step()` calls re-sets-up the model like `solve()` does. The model's value is only written after the "already initialised for another model" check, so that `RuntimeError` leaves it unchanged.

**One addition you didn't ask for:** with `calc_ic=False`, the algebraic sensitivities at a restart are now recomputed from the algebraic equations. Without this, the stored sensitivity at the restart point was stale (1 instead of 5 in my test), even though later points were right.

**Checks:** finite differences confirm the experiment sensitivities in both `"legacy"` and `"unified"` modes, including with an input maximum concentration, which used to raise `AttributeError`. Results with no discontinuities or sensitivities match the original code exactly, at the same speed.

**Two things to know:**
- Sensitivities with respect to a switch time itself (e.g. `d/d t_switch`) are still zero. That's the limitation the docstrings already mention, and I didn't change it.
- Input sets whose discontinuities fall at different times still raise "Discontinuity events occur at different times", as the existing test expects.

I also added 45 tests (in `test_idaklu_solver.py`, `test_base_solver.py` and `test_simulation_with_experiment.py`) and a CHANGELOG bullet, which has no PR link because there's no PR number yet. These are outside `src/pybamm`, so they'll be discarded along with any other changes outside it. To run the tests here I had to put stand-ins for the missing `hypothesis` and `pytest-mock` packages in `/tmp`, outside the repository.
